title: HB 1239 (112th General Assembly): AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 2, relative to fingerprint identification of voters.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) new section in Title 2, Chapter 1 (Sec. 1(a))
(quote) (a) The state election commission and each county election commission may utilize technology to identify the fingerprints of voters for purposes of conducting elections in this state in accordance with this title.
(b_no_id_remedy) not stated.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule) not stated.
(other) Sec. 1(b): each state agency with a fingerprint database, including the Tennessee bureau of investigation, must work with the secretary of state to carry out the section.
(other) Sec. 2: takes effect on becoming law.
(other) version: 2287633-Draft: Draft only; permissive fingerprint identification of voters. It does not say fingerprints replace or add to the 2-7-112(c) list, or what a voter must do.
(other) note: Only the Draft is saved. Companion SB1162 is not in this group. Last action: sponsors added 2021-03-15 while in House Elections & Campaign Finance Subcommittee; no roll call saved.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
